attacks.claim: Admin actions that delete data, flip the kill switch, or enforce the budget stop have no described authorization or audit trail. Anyone able to write server config or trigger deletes is not constrained by the artifact.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: who can write cross_save_enabled or trigger restores and deletes, and whether those actions are logged. Artifact says 'Kill switch cross_save_enabled=false (server config...)'.

attacks.claim: Linking has no described protection against concurrent requests that could both pass the one-link-per-account check, and this race is not in the QA table.
attacks.evidence: 'Each store account can be in at most one link.' QA lists only 'Linking an account already in a link | Refused', a sequential case.

attacks.claim: The client trusts the blob checksum, which is stored inside the blob and so proves integrity but not authenticity. A well-formed blob still reaches the save parser.
attacks.evidence: 'The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading'; ABSENT: a signed or server-side authenticity check on blobs.

attacks.claim: sync.meta includes a device name, which can contain a real name, but the stored-data list omits it and claims no personal data beyond IDs.
attacks.evidence: 'sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)' vs 'We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID, save blobs, sync.meta. No email, name, payment or friends data.'

attacks.claim: Retention of the persistent steam_id to epic_account_id link is unspecified. That link is a cross-platform identifier and remains linkable after cloud data is deleted.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention for link rows. Artifact gives only 'Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted' and 'removes the link and all server copies'.

attacks.claim: The backend host and vendor are not named, and there is no export or migration path for save data. Exit cost is unassessed.
attacks.evidence: 'Storage region: EU (Frankfurt) for all players.' ABSENT: hosting provider, save export, exit plan.

attacks.claim: A sync uploads all slots, but the upload limit is 60 per hour. A few routine launches can exhaust it, and throttled syncs then count toward the 2% error alert.
attacks.evidence: '10 slots per player, and 60 uploads per hour per player' with 'sync uploads the existing save slots'. ABSENT: behaviour and messaging when rate-limited.

attacks.claim: The load test (30k concurrent launches in 10 min) is not tied to the expected patch-day peak. Everyone may launch 1.4 in the same window.
attacks.evidence: 'Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors' vs 'Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores'. ABSENT: expected peak derivation.

attacks.claim: The storage forecast does not follow from the stated limits. 60% of about 182k players is about 109k, times 10 slots, times 5 versions, times 420 KB, which is about 2.3 TB, not about 140 GB.
attacks.evidence: '~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month.'

attacks.claim: The budget stop mechanism is unspecified. The $250 alert only notifies, billing data lags, and the 'hard' stop and automatic kill-switch flip are asserted without a described implementation.
attacks.evidence: 'Cloud billing alert at $250/month and hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically.' ABSENT: how the stop is enforced and tested.

attacks.claim: No alert covers save-loss signals: version pruning, rejected blobs, conflict timeouts, or silent overwrite. The alerts are error rate, 5xx, and restore spikes compared to a 2,450-player beta.
attacks.evidence: 'Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate.' ABSENT: alert on checksum or schema rejections or on server version pruning.

attacks.claim: Reverting to 1.3 through the default branch does not downgrade players who already installed 1.4. Only the Steam beta branch was tested, Epic downgrade was not tested, and the kill switch and automatic budget flip are absent from the QA table.
attacks.evidence: '1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores' vs QA 'Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch 1.3-legacy)'. The kill-switch row is ABSENT from the QA table.

attacks.claim: All players receive 1.4 at once, with no staged percentage rollout. A client-side save bug in the gameplay additions or bug fixes reaches 182k players before store rollback can take effect.
attacks.evidence: 'Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores; Cross-Save available to everyone who turns it on.' ABSENT: staged rollout plan.

attacks.claim: The server keeps only 5 versions per slot and never parses blobs. A buggy client that uploads well-formed but wrong saves five times irreversibly prunes every good version.
attacks.evidence: 'the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot' and 'the server never parses them'. ABSENT: pinning of known-good versions or server-side sanity checks.

attacks.claim: After a 1.3 round trip, sync.meta is stale because 1.3 ignores it and may rewrite the slot without the modifier keys. A later 1.4 comparison can then silently overwrite progress, contrary to the stated guarantee.
attacks.evidence: '1.3 ignores the sidecar, so a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save' and 'Nothing is overwritten without that choice.' ABSENT: QA case of 1.3 save followed by 1.4 relaunch.

attacks.claim: The rules for 'changed since last sync' and 'newest' are undefined. If wall-clock last-modified timestamps from different PCs decide, clock skew can make an older save look newer and be overwritten without a prompt.
attacks.evidence: 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.' ABSENT: change-detection baseline and how timestamps are compared across devices.

attacks.claim: If the newest cloud blob is well-formed but unloadable, the artifact describes no path to supersede it, so each launch may fail or re-prompt indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: 'a blob that fails is not loaded, the previous version is kept' ABSENT: how a bad newest cloud copy is replaced or recovered.

attacks.claim: The claim that players must never lose a save rests on zero losses across 2,450 Steam beta and 150 Epic sandbox testers. The Epic production path was never exercised, and QA ran on private-branch builds.
attacks.evidence: '0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts' and 'Epic sandbox testers (150)'; 'Steam build 18204411 on a private branch'.

attacks.claim: The public patch note promises that saves stay where they are, but first sync can replace the local save with a newer cloud copy.
attacks.evidence: Patch note: 'Your saves on this PC stay where they are.' vs 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.'

attacks.claim: Checked, nothing gate-worthy: the value case (continue on either store) is stated and the feature is opt-in.
attacks.evidence: 'continue the same save on either store. Off until a player turns it on in Settings > Cross-Save.'

attacks.claim: The 'unlink first' refusal is a dead end when the existing link belongs to an account the player cannot access, and no recovery path is described.
attacks.evidence: 'Linking an account already in a link | Refused with "unlink first" message' ABSENT: recovery path when the link is not under the player's control.

attacks.claim: Screen narration is verified only for the conflict prompt. The sync status line and error and offline messages are not stated as tested.
attacks.evidence: 'screen narration for the conflict prompt | Pass' vs 'Cross-Save: offline, will sync later'. ABSENT: narration checks for the status and error strings.

attacks.claim: Child-data handling covers only Epic cabined accounts. Steam-side age handling is absent, and the consent step is described as a privacy-policy link rather than an affirmative consent.
attacks.evidence: 'Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered' ABSENT: Steam under-13 handling. 'linked from the Cross-Save screen before linking' ABSENT: consent action.

attacks.claim: The claim that Steam requires no listing change is asserted without a policy check or reference.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam requires no listing change.' ABSENT: Steam policy review reference.

attacks.claim: Cross-Save is bundled with two modifiers and 31 bug fixes, so there is no independent kill switch for the modifiers and rollback is all-or-nothing.
attacks.evidence: 'Two new difficulty modifiers and 31 bug fixes' alongside the single 'cross_save_enabled' kill switch.

attacks.claim: Checked, nothing gate-worthy beyond the items above.

attacks.claim: Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted automatically. A player whose only remaining copy is in the cloud, for example after a reinstall or new PC, loses that save with no notice. This directly violates the agreed 'players must never lose a save' rule.
attacks.evidence: Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted; if that player launches again, local saves are simply uploaded fresh.

attacks.claim: The server keeps only 5 versions per slot and does not parse blobs, and the artifact never says the client validates a save before uploading it. A corrupt or bad local save can become the newest cloud version and push out the last good versions after 5 syncs.
attacks.evidence: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot ... the server never parses them

attacks.claim: The auto-download rule overwrites the local save based on client-written last-modified times, with no prompt. Because 1.3 ignores the sidecar, progress made on 1.3 does not update it, so 1.4 can later treat the local save as older and silently replace it. Device clock skew can also make the 'newest' choice wrong. This contradicts the stated guarantee.
attacks.evidence: On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older. ... Nothing is overwritten without that choice.

attacks.claim: Age gating is specified only for Epic cabined accounts. Steam accounts of under-13 or minor players can link and sync personal identifiers and save data with no stated age check or parental consent path, which is a children's-data risk for an EU-hosted store.

attacks.evidence: Epic cabined test account | Linking not offered, explanation shown (ABSENT: server-side refusal test for restricted EOS status)

attacks.claim: The rollback relies on restoring 1.3 as the default branch on both stores. The only downgrade test used the opt-in beta branch '1.3-legacy'. Players already on 1.4 are not shown to be moved back, and the default-branch promotion path is untested.
attacks.evidence: 1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores; ... Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)
